problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}],\,{e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5t} & t{e}^{5t} \\ 0 & {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]
$$

Given the matrices $A$ and ${e}^{At}$ above, compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{At}).$

| $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{At})=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{At})=A\,{e}^{At}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{At}) & =A\,{e}^{At} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{5t} & t{e}^{5t} \\ 0 & {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{5t} & (5t+1){e}^{5t} \\ 0 & 5{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
